events.text:
🇷🇺🇺🇦🇺🇸🇰🇿🛢 Novorossiysk, There Air Defense, U.S. Worries On Oil Profits:
KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukrainian anti-ship missiles, jet-powered aerial drones and sea drones blitzed a major Russian naval base on the Black Sea coast in a “unique” nighttime operation, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Wednesday.
Cutting-edge drones developed by Kyiv since Russia invaded more than four years ago have repeatedly targeted Russian ships in the Black Sea, including warships and oil tankers. Both countries have Black Sea shorelines.
Ukraine’s uncrewed fleet has succeeded in limiting the movements of Russia’s once-dominant Black Sea navy, Kyiv officials say, in one of the country’s biggest feats of the war.
But Ukrainian officials reckon that Russian President Vladimir Putin is bent on prosecuting the invasion, despite his bigger army’s slow and costly progress on the battlefield and U.S. diplomatic efforts to find a settlement.
Putin is planning “an additional rapid mobilization of several hundred thousand Russians by the end of the year,” Zelenskyy said on social media late Tuesday, citing Ukrainian intel.
Those reports have also said recently that Russia is expanding production of ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, both of which are hard for Ukrainian air defenses to counter.
Meanwhile, Ukraine is also trying to scale up its weapons manufacturing through agreements with partner countries, as both countries apparently plan to fight on.
The Ukrainian military “carried out a unique operation targeting the naval base in Novorossiysk — the last major stronghold of the Russian fleet in the Black Sea,” Zelenskyy said in a social media post.
The attack struck air defenses, piers and other port infrastructure in the Krasnodar region city, he added.
Krasnodar region Gov. Veniamin Kondratyev said that hundreds of Ukrainian drones attacked Novorossiysk, Anapa and Gelendzhik and the Temryuk district overnight.
Novorossiysk is also home to a key international oil terminal. The Grushovaya oil transshipment complex near Novorossiysk is one of the largest transshipment hubs in southern Russia for oil and petroleum products.
Last Feb, the U.S. State Department expressed its displeasure about Ukraine’s attacks on Novorossiysk, saying they have impacted U.S. oil interests in ⁠Kazakhstan.
The Caspian Pipeline Consortium operates a pipeline from the Caspian coast in northwest Kazakhstan to Novorossiysk. The pipeline handles much of the crude exports from three major Kazakh fields in which major U.S. energy companies, Chevron and ExxonMobil, have stakes.
In illegally annexed Crimea, air defenses downed 115 Ukrainian drones over Sevastopol overnight, the city’s Russia-appointed head said, adding that 10 apartment buildings and 25 private houses were damaged.
Russian air defenses downed more than 500 Ukrainian drones Moscow said.
In Novorossiysk, an eight-year old child was killed in the attack, and a person wounded when his house in the Temryuk region was hit later died in hospital, Kondratyev said. He added that 12 other people in the region were wounded.
Debris from downed drones fell on the territory of four industrial plants and 21 residential buildings, according to Kondratyev, but officials gave no details of any damage.
Meanwhile, Ukraine’s air force said Wednesday that Russia fired 138 long-range strike drones as well as an unspecified number of missiles at Ukraine during the night. Damage was recorded at 16 locations across the country, it said.
In the southern Kherson region of Ukraine, a large-scale Russian drone attack overnight killed two people and wounded two others, regional head Oleksandr Prokudin said Wednesday.
The attacks also destroyed a shopping mall in the southern Ukraine city of Zaporizhzhia.
---
However, U.S. leadership is pushing back, specifically Vance and Trump, as they are concerned about American companies' financial connections to Russia and Kazakhstan's oil trade. More in next post.

⚡🇱🇧🇸🇾13 years ago,on August 15, 2013,a devastating explosion rocked the heart of Beirut, carrying a message of terror intended to break the resilience of the people and plunge Lebanon into strife.
Martyrs fell and the streets were scarred by destruction, but the true takeaway was clear: Lebanon would not wait for terrorism to reach its doorstep.
As terrorist groups expanded along the Syrian border and in the rugged outskirts (Jurud), the decision was taken to confront the threat head-on.
 Resistance fighters advanced into the hard-to-reach strongholds of these armed groups, fighting harsh battles until the militants were forced to retreat beyond the Syrian border.
This fight was never about defending a single region or sect it was a battle for all of Lebanon. From the blood-stained streets of the Southern Suburbs to the high ridges along the border where the banners of victory were raised, the objective remained constant: to drive terrorism away and keep Lebanon’s borders and people safe.

Assembly of the multipurpose vessel is expected to take 36 months to complete, with state defense firm Viettel Group alongside state military factories supplying most of the warship’s weapons, components, and battle management capabilities.
The surface combatant will incorporate an active electronically scanned array radar, air-defense and anti-ship missiles, torpedo launchers, and a flight deck for a maritime helicopter.

🇮🇷🇧🇭 Iran's opening salvo: Bahrain base strike sparked US carrier supply crisis
The supply issues plaguing the USS Abraham Lincoln and other maritime forces in the Iran war stem from the destruction of the US Fifth Fleet base in Bahrain, according to the NYT. 
➡️ Iranian missiles and drones[ struck the base on the first day of the conflict](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65551), eliminating the primary supply point the navy has relied on for decades and forcing a scramble for alternatives 
➡️ The other major maritime logistics hub, Fujairah in the UAE, is also well within range of Iranian missiles
➡️ As a result, the Pentagon turned to Diego Garcia, a British-controlled island in the Indian Ocean roughly 2,200 miles from where the carrier strike groups were operating
➡️ The base has since become the main logistics hub for[ the US Navy's operations in the region](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67050). The shift may explain why Iran attacked the island with ballistic missiles in March 
The loss of the Bahrain hub has contributed to a host of reported problems on carriers operating against Iran, with media outlets citing shortages of basic supplies and [deteriorating mental health ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73343)among crew members. 
The Lincoln was on a scheduled deployment from San Diego when it was redirected to the Middle East in January and has been extended multiple times without a clear end date. Some of the crew have been told they will not return home until 2027, while the carrier has now gone 250 days without a port visit.
The Pentagon has turned to Diego Garcia as an alternative, but it is far from the operating area and lacks the infrastructure and supplies needed to support a carrier group. The supply chain is so stretched that some essential items are flown in on military cargo planes rather than shipped by sea, rendering[ the blockade of Iran a painfully Sisyphean task.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73394)

🇮🇷🚢 Shipments around Persian Gulf completely paralyzed
The security situation in the Persian Gulf has entered a more dangerous phase, as the US blockade of Iranian ports coincides with targeted Iranian and Houthi attacks at both key chokepoints, according to maritime intelligence group Marisks.
➡️ These two routes, which carry the bulk of energy exports from the Gulf, can no longer be assessed independently. Pressure at Hormuz is diverting traffic toward Saudi Arabia's Red Sea outlets, while Houthi attacks simultaneously threaten that alternative, leaving shipping with no viable workaround
➡️ The shipping industry has responded by turning off transponders to avoid detection. In the three weeks since the US blockade was reimposed, more than half of all tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz have gone dark
For Gulf states, the economic pain is compounded by the loss of shipping revenue and the rising cost of war risk insurance, which has increased premiums by more than 500% for vessels transiting the region. With no safe passage available, the global economy is beginning to feel the strain of a crisis that shows no signs of abating.

👹🇮🇱US presses Netanyahu to condemn settler siege of Palestinian homes
The Trump administration is urging Benjamin Netanyahu to issue clear public condemnation of the actions of [the militant settlers](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73353), reports Reuters.
The pressure intensified after the White House learned that one of the targeted homes belongs to a Palestinian-American, a US official and an Israeli official are cited as saying.
Even US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee - normally a vocal supporter of Jewish settlement activity - on Thursday labeled the settlers “Israeli terrorists.”
For nearly a week, settlers have [encircled homes ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73330)in the village of Qusra.
🔶 They sealed off the road to three houses and pitched a tent in the front yards, blocking anyone from entering or leaving
🔶 They earlier cut electricity and water supplies
🔶 Some 15 Palestinians, including two children, have been trapped inside without running water or power
Foreign and Israeli activists delivered limited aid - food, bottled water, and canned goods - on Friday, but the IDF that arrived on Thursday barred them from reaching the homes directly, declaring the area a closed military zone for non-residents.
What is happening in Qusra is part of a systematic, calculated strategy by extremist settlers and the Israeli government to seize Palestinian land in the occupied West Bank.
👉 According to rights groups, settlers are attempting to seize properties on the outskirts of Qusra and neighboring Jalud in order to connect them with nearby larger settlements in classic land-grab tactics.
Under the official pretext of stopping escalating settler attacks, the IDF has been extensively using [a new military decree](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73395) and declaring areas a "closed military zone", in effect allowing settler attacks to continue with impunity.
Netanyahu’s government has aggressively accelerated settlement expansion in land Israel captured in 1967, establishing dozens of new settlements and outposts.
Public condemnation just two months before an election could alienate the settler movement - a powerful voting bloc that forms a crucial pillar of Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition.

🇷🇺🇨🇳 How Russia and China turn Arctic into working trade corridor
Russia and China are giving the Arctic route something it has long lacked - regular commercial traffic.
Chinese shipping companies are expanding operations along Russia’s Northern Sea Route, with at least six operators reportedly planning more than 50 voyages this season, mostly between Russian and Chinese ports.
🚢 Sea Legend is preparing a seasonal China-Europe container service with an advertised transit time of around 20 days, while New New Shipping has opened a route linking Tianjin with Murmansk.
Energy is part of the same picture. Russian LNG is increasingly moving through the route toward Chinese markets.
China heads north
Beijing’s Arctic interest is not new. Under its “Polar Silk Road” concept, China has long viewed northern shipping lanes as a possible extension of its trade network, while Chinese companies invested in projects such as Yamal LNG and Arctic LNG 2.
❌ For years, however, harsh conditions, high costs and limited traffic kept those ambitions modest.
That started to change after 2022, when Western companies pulled back from several Russian Arctic projects. Russia needed new buyers, capital and logistics partners; China wanted secure energy supplies and greater access to northern routes.
New Arctic landscape
👉 China is no longer simply buying Russian resources. Its shipping companies are gaining practical experience operating along the NSR, building knowledge of Arctic navigation, logistics and seasonal trade. At the same time, the route is beginning to support two-way trade: Chinese goods are moving north toward Russia while Russian raw materials travel in the opposite direction, gradually turning the Northern Sea Route into a more integrated trade corridor.
Disruptions around the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz have shown how quickly conflict can interfere with global energy and shipping flows, giving Russia and China another reason to develop alternative routes outside the most exposed regions.
While traffic along the Northern Sea Route remains small compared with established global routes, the direction of change is clear - Chinese and Russian economic interests are increasingly intertwined.
